### Xbox static recompilation for Nintendo Switch and Linux The original Xbox (NTSC-U) release of **Burnout 3: Takedown**, lifted instruction by instruction to C and running natively, with no emulator. ![Switch](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nintendo%20Switch-homebrew-E60012?logo=nintendoswitch&logoColor=white) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x86__64-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vulkan-1.3-AC162C?logo=vulkan&logoColor=white) ![OpenGL](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenGL-renderer-5586A4?logo=opengl&logoColor=white) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2-blue) [Features](#-features) · [Playing on Switch](#%EF%B8%8F-playing-on-switch) · [Building](#%EF%B8%8F-building) · [Configuration](#%EF%B8%8F-configuration) · [Status](#-status)
--- > [!IMPORTANT] > **No game data is included.** You need your own copy of the Xbox disc, > extracted (`default.xbe`, `Data/`, `Tracks/`, `ovid/`, `pveh/`, `sound/`, ...). Built on the runtime of the NFS Underground 2 / Carbon Switch ports (GPU renderers, Horizon support). An upstream Windows port with a software GPU exists at [sp00nznet/burnout3](https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3). ## ✨ Features - 🏁 **Native code**: the whole game runs as recompiled C, built with [xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp) - 🎮 **Two renderers**: Vulkan (NVK on Switch) and OpenGL, with render scaling - 🌆 **The full 3D world**: races, the car-select garage, motion blur and bloom (the game's off-screen scene composite), fog - 🪞 **Car reflections** (Vulkan): the game's dynamic reflection cube with its light-strip highlights - 🖼️ **Picture options** in **Driver Details → Settings → Gameplay** (Vulkan): **Resolution Scale** 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 2.5x, **Anti-Aliasing** (FXAA) and **Anisotropic Filtering** Off-16x, applied at once and kept in `b3x_options.txt`; mipmaps with trilinear filtering - ⏱️ **Real-time races at any frame rate**: the game steps its simulation by the time that really passed instead of one 60 Hz step per frame, so races below 60 fps are not slow motion - 🔊 **Audio** through an emulated Xbox APU (engine, effects, EA Trax, speech), 5.1 downmixed to stereo - 🎬 **Movies** (XMV) with a native colour converter - 💾 **Profiles** save and load (`game/UDATA`), including after racing ## 🕹️ Playing on Switch 1. Copy the NRO to `sdmc:/switch/b3x/` (`b3x-vulkan.nro` for the Vulkan build, `b3x.nro` for OpenGL). 2. Copy the **extracted** disc (not the ISO) to `sdmc:/switch/b3x/game/`. 3. Start it with **title takeover**: hold **R** while launching any game. Applet mode leaves too little memory. ``` sdmc:/switch/b3x/ ├── b3x-vulkan.nro ├── b3x_env.txt optional settings, KEY=VALUE per line ├── b3x_options.txt written by the in-game picture options └── game/ ├── default.xbe ├── UDATA/ your profiles └── ... ``` Buttons map by label (Switch A = Xbox A). Settings go in `b3x_env.txt` (see [Configuration](#%EF%B8%8F-configuration)) and the log is written to the same folder (`b3x_log.txt`). ## 🛠️ Building
1. Lift the XBE to C ```sh # Writes B3_GEN_DIR (default /root/b3x/gen) B3_XBE=/path/to/game/default.xbe B3_GEN_DIR=/path/to/gen tools/regen.sh ```
2a. Linux (SDL2 + OpenGL or Vulkan) ```sh cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DNFSU2_GEN_DIR=/path/to/gen # add -DNFSU2_VULKAN=ON for Vulkan cmake --build build NFSU2_GAME_DIR=/path/to/game build/b3_recomp ```
2b. Nintendo Switch (devkitA64, switch-sdl2, switch-mesa) ```sh NFSU2_GEN_DIR=/path/to/gen NFSU2_GAME_SRC=/path/to/game switch/build.sh # Vulkan build (needs mesa-switch NVK and glslang for Switch) VULKAN=1 JOBS=6 NFSU2_GEN_DIR=/path/to/gen switch/build.sh ```
### Project layout | Path | What | |---|---| | `src/main.c` | boot and runtime defaults | | `src/recomp_manual.c` | hand-written overrides of lifted functions (library hooks, XMV colour converter, simulation stepping, the Gameplay picture rows) | | `src/switch_nx.c` | Switch log device, env file, exception handler, loading screen | | `config/seed_functions.json` | entry points the static pass cannot see | | `xboxrecomp/` | the toolkit (MIT), vendored with this port's changes: NV2A renderers (Vulkan, OpenGL), SDL audio, Switch platform layer, translator fixes | | `tools/regen.sh` | XBE → lifted C (`gen/`, never committed) | | `switch/build.sh` | Switch NRO build + SD-card staging | ## ⚙️ Configuration On Linux these are ordinary environment variables. On the Switch they go in `sdmc:/switch/b3x/b3x_env.txt`, one `KEY=VALUE` per line (`#` starts a comment). Anything left out runs at its default. Most of the list is for debugging, so the sections below are folded. ```ini # sdmc:/switch/b3x/b3x_env.txt RECOMP_GL_SCALE=1.5 NFSU2_CPU_MHZ=1785 ```
Build and code generation | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `XBOXRECOMP_DIR` | Toolkit to build or regenerate with (default: the vendored `xboxrecomp/`). | | `B3_XBE` | `default.xbe` to lift (`tools/regen.sh`). | | `B3_GEN_DIR` / `NFSU2_GEN_DIR` | Directory for the lifted C (default `/root/b3x/gen`). | | `LIFT_ONLY=1` | `regen.sh`: only re-lift (enough after translator or `recomp_manual.c` changes; seed changes need the full run). | | `TRACE_FUNCS` | `regen.sh`: JSON list of addresses whose entries are logged (`[TRACE]`). | | `NFSU2_GAME_SRC` | `switch/build.sh`: extracted disc to stage (default `/root/b3x/game`). | | `SD_ROOT` | `switch/build.sh`: staging SD-card root (default `/switch_sd`). | | `BUILD_DIR` | `switch/build.sh`: build directory (default `/root/b3x/build-switch`, `-vk` with `VULKAN=1`). | | `JOBS` | `switch/build.sh`: parallel compile jobs (6 fits `-O2` in RAM). | | `VULKAN=1` | `switch/build.sh`: build the Vulkan renderer (`b3x-vulkan.nro`). | | `NVK_SDK`, `GLSLANG_DIR` | `switch/build.sh` with `VULKAN=1`: mesa-switch NVK install and Switch glslang. | | `LTO=1` | `switch/build.sh`: link-time optimisation of the lifted code. |
Game and host | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `NFSU2_GAME_DIR` | Extracted disc (Linux; default `./game`). The Switch always uses `sdmc:/switch/b3x/game/`. | | `NFSU2_GL=0` | Use the executor's CPU renderer instead of the GPU renderer. | | `NFSU2_APU=0` | No emulated APU (no sound). | | `B3_FRAME_LOCK=1` | One simulation step per rendered frame, as on the Xbox (races go slow motion below 60 fps). | | `NFSU2_EXIT_TRACE=1` | Print the guest state at exit. |
Switch (Horizon) | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `NFSU2_CPU_MHZ`, `NFSU2_GPU_MHZ`, `NFSU2_MEM_MHZ` | Clocks (opt-in; more heat and battery). The log shows `[clock] ...`. | | `NFSU2_NO_LOG=1` / `NFSU2_LOG=0` | No log file, no `[perf]` reports, no profiler. | | `NFSU2_LOG_SYNC=1` | Write every log line to the card at once (slow; for hangs). | | `NFSU2_LOADER=0` | No loading screen before the first frame. | | `RECOMP_NX_PROFILE` | Sampling profiler into `prof.bin`: 1 = busy threads, 2 = every thread above 2%. | | `RECOMP_NX_AUDIO_PRIO=0` | Leave the audio threads at the default priority. |
Scheduling and kernel | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `RECOMP_GIL_EAGER=1` | Hand the guest lock over by guest priority. | | `RECOMP_VBLANK` | Vblank interrupt for D3D (default 1). | | `RECOMP_NO_MIRRORS=1` | Map no RAM mirrors (what the Switch does; for reproducing it on a desktop). | | `RECOMP_QUIET` | 1 = no periodic kernel/GPU summaries (Switch default), 0 = show them. | | `XBOX_LOG_LEVEL` | Kernel log level (0 errors … trace). |
Graphics (GL and Vulkan renderers) | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `RECOMP_GL_SCALE` | Render resolution multiple (fractions allowed). Vulkan: only until Gameplay → Resolution Scale is changed. | | `RECOMP_GL_THREAD=1` | GL renderer: GL calls on their own thread. | | `RECOMP_PROG_CACHE` | Shader/pipeline cache file, `=0` off. | | `RECOMP_CULL=0` | No off-screen batch culling (the port's default). | | `RECOMP_VK_MIPS=0` | Vulkan: no mipmaps. | | `RECOMP_VK_ANISO` | Vulkan: anisotropic filtering cap, 1..16. | | `RECOMP_VK_LOD_BIAS` | Vulkan: mip bias, negative = sharper (default -0.25). | | `RECOMP_VK_FXAA=0` | Vulkan: no FXAA. | | `RECOMP_VK_SQUARE=0` | Vulkan: in 16:9, no extra 4/3 columns for square pixels. | | `RECOMP_VK_CUBE=0` | Vulkan: no reflection cube maps. | | `RECOMP_VK_HEADLESS=1` | Vulkan on Linux: no window (also implied by `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen`). | | `RECOMP_VK_VALIDATION=1` | Vulkan on Linux: Khronos validation layer. | | `RECOMP_GL_DUMP=[,every]` | Write presented frames as BMP (every N frames, default 60). | | `RECOMP_VK_DUMP_SURF=[,...]` | Vulkan: also dump these surfaces with each dumped frame; `RECOMP_VK_DUMP_RAW=1` adds BGRA files with alpha. | | `RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE=` | When the file exists: one line per draw/clear of the next frame (target, state, textures, combiner, first vertices). | | `RECOMP_FPS_LOG=1` | Presented frames per 10 s. |
Audio | Variable | Meaning | |---|---| | `RECOMP_AUDIO=0` | No host audio device. | | `RECOMP_AUDIO_VOLUME` | Master volume 0..100. | | `RECOMP_AUDIO_DUMP=,,` | Record the exact PCM sent to the device. | | `RECOMP_APU_VOICES=1` | Every APU voice of the last 5 s (format, bins, buffer, peak). | | `RECOMP_APU_TRACE=1` | Front-end methods and a per-second voice summary. |
## 📊 Status | | | |---|---| | Intro movies, title, menus | ✅ working | | Profile create / save / load | ✅ working (saves after racing fixed in 0.1) | | 3D world: races, garage, motion blur, reflections | ✅ working (GL has no reflections) | | Audio: music, engine, effects | ✅ working | | Races at real-time speed below 60 fps | ✅ working | | Picture options (Vulkan) | ✅ working | | Race training videos | ⚠️ play in full before an event's first race (cannot be skipped) | | Switch | 🧪 runs on hardware (Vulkan), 40-55 fps in races; being tuned | See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

# The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age — Recomp

[![Local milestone](https://img.shields.io/badge/local%20milestone-menu%20%2B%20audio%20verified-brightgreen)](docs/STATUS.md)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078D4?logo=windows)](https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp)
[![Original hardware](https://img.shields.io/badge/original%20hardware-Xbox-107C10?logo=xbox)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_(console))
[![Language](https://img.shields.io/github/languages/top/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp)](https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp)
[![CMake](https://img.shields.io/badge/CMake-3.20%2B-064F8C?logo=cmake)](CMakeLists.txt)
[![Local audio checks](https://img.shields.io/badge/local%20audio%20checks-5455%20passing-brightgreen)](docs/STATUS.md#verification)
[![Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp)](https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp/issues)
[![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp)](https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp/commits/main)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp?style=flat)](https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp/stargazers)

An early-stage static recompilation of the North American original-Xbox release
of *The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age* (`EA-095`, title ID `4541005F`,
version 8) into a native Windows executable.

This repository contains project-specific source code and research only. It
does **not** contain the game executable, disc image, movies, audio, or other
copyrighted game assets. You must supply files from a legally owned copy.

## Current status

**Startup reaches the main menu with working audio. Gameplay is not yet
verified.** Status reviewed October 9, 2026.

These milestones describe the menu/audio source checkpoint and its matching
runtime submodule revision. Game-code generation is still a local step, so a
fresh clone is not yet a turnkey build. The local-checks badge is a recorded
result, not a GitHub Actions/CI status.

- Loads the original XBE sections and resolves the title's 117 kernel imports.
- Renders the loading ring, legal splash/logo, EA, THX and New Line movies,
  followed by a textured main menu in the diagnostic framebuffer window.
- Completes the startup command queue in roughly 38 seconds on the development
  machine; this is an observation, not a performance guarantee.
- Produces audible movie and menu audio. A listener reports clean THX, New Line
  and main-menu music after the audio pacing correction.
- Passes 5,455 local APU regression checks in both Debug and Release, covering
  sample delivery, mixer advancement, IRQ status, voice-table backing and
  audio-thread lifecycle.

The next milestone is **New Game → opening scene → first controllable
gameplay**, checking input, transitions, 3D rendering, dialogue and effects.
Broader rendering, voice resampling, DSP effects and audio/video synchronization
remain unverified. Slight roughness in the EA logo audio needs a source/emulator
comparison before being classified as a bug. See [project status](docs/STATUS.md).

## Documentation

- [Status, limitations and next milestone](docs/STATUS.md)
- [First working-audio checkpoint](docs/WORKING_AUDIO_CHECKPOINT.md)
- [Front-end investigation and latest verification](docs/FRONTEND_STATE_TRACE.md)
- [Native/emulator startup comparison](docs/STARTUP_COMPARISON.md)
- [Disc intake and historical bring-up](docs/INTAKE.md)

## Repository layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` | Game-specific host entry point and manual recompilation overrides |
| `config/` | Validated analysis seeds |
| `docs/` | Intake notes and technical findings |
| `vendor/xboxrecomp/` | Pinned public runtime/tooling fork |
| `dump/` | Local game executable, extracted assets, and analysis output (ignored) |
| `src/recomp/` | Locally generated recompilation sources (ignored) |

## Requirements

- 64-bit Windows
- Visual Studio 2022 with the Desktop development with C++ workload
- CMake 3.20 or newer
- Python 3 with the runtime/tooling dependencies for local analysis and generation
- Git with submodule support
- A legally owned North American Xbox copy of the game

## Setup

Clone the project and its runtime:

```powershell
git clone --recursive https://github.com/Revan67/ThirdAge-Recomp.git
cd ThirdAge-Recomp
```

Extract your own disc so the executable is located at:

```text
dump/game_files/default.xbe
```

The rest of the extracted disc filesystem belongs beneath
`dump/game_files/` as well. Game data is intentionally excluded by
`.gitignore` and must never be committed or redistributed.

Generated files under `src/recomp/` are also kept local. The analysis and
generation workflow is still being stabilized, so a fresh clone is not yet a
one-command reproducible build. Use the matching pinned runtime revision.
Do not substitute an arbitrary newer upstream runtime for the pinned revision.
Once those sources have been generated and the matching runtime is available, build
with:

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release
.\build\Release\third_age_recomp.exe
```

Run from the repository root so the relative game-data paths resolve correctly.
This is a development build, not an installable release. Diagnostic runs should
be bounded and stopped afterward; closing a window must not trigger a relaunch
loop.

## Local regression checks

The current working runtime includes a deterministic audio suite with a silent
fake output sink; it does not require game data or play audio through speakers:

```powershell
cmake -S vendor/xboxrecomp/tests/apu_monitor -B build/tests/apu_monitor -A x64
cmake --build build/tests/apu_monitor --config Release --target apu_monitor_test
.\build\tests\apu_monitor\Release\apu_monitor_test.exe
```

Use `Debug` in both paths/configuration to check that build too. These test
sources are included in the matching runtime submodule revision.
Additional renderer/compiler checks are described in the
[verification notes](docs/STATUS.md#verification).

## Verified reference input

The current research uses a disc matching these Redump values:

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Disc size | `7,825,162,240` bytes |
| Disc MD5 | `57e3789289a89c860067d3c770e61807` |
| Disc SHA-1 | `bc97495b5702b11c4ae2c0e53d47ab1844dd3e4b` |
| `default.xbe` SHA-256 | `a45ca85284a12b86877ebe37e9e86741f166207bfc5a4355df990fa341a2485d` |

These hashes identify the supported input; they are not links to game data.

## Privacy and repository policy

Disc dumps, extracted assets, generated binaries, logs, saves, local tools,
editor settings, credentials, signing keys, and machine-specific files stay
outside version control. Before opening a pull request, check `git status` and
confirm that no proprietary or personal data is staged.

The runtime is a separate Git checkout: its changes must be reviewed and
published before updating the parent repository's submodule pointer. A dirty
submodule alone does not carry runtime fixes into a clone.

## Licensing

No project-root license has been selected yet. The runtime has its own
[license and third-party notices](vendor/xboxrecomp/LICENSE); those do not
automatically assign a license to this project's original files. No game-data
distribution permission is implied.

## Disclaimer

This is an independent preservation and compatibility research project. It is
not affiliated with or endorsed by Electronic Arts, Warner Bros., Tolkien
Enterprises, Microsoft, or the original developers. No game assets are
provided.

releases.name: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 v0.3.1 - Linux Timing and AppImage Compatibility
releases.body:
## Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 v0.3.1 - Linux Timing and AppImage Compatibility

v0.3.1 is a small update after v0.3.0. It fixes the game speed when the Linux build cannot hold 60 FPS, makes the Linux AppImage start on older systems, and opens a launcher window when Vulkan cannot start. This is an unofficial fan-made port, not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's makers or publishers.

**No game files are included.** You need your own Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 Xbox Live Arcade package.

### Linux timing

- At the **60 FPS** setting, a frame that misses one or more vblanks now advances the game by the number of 1/60 steps that really passed (at most three), instead of always one. A computer that renders around 30 FPS no longer makes the game itself run at half speed. The picture is less smooth, but the game keeps its speed.
- A frame on time still gets exactly the game's original step. The 30, 90 and higher frame rates keep their existing timing.

**This does not make the Linux frame rate faster.** Why some Linux systems render around 30 FPS ([#1](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues/1)) is still under investigation. The timing fix has automated tests but has **not yet been confirmed** on the Steam Machine from that report.

### Linux / AppImage

- **A launcher window when Vulkan is unavailable.** If Vulkan cannot start (no driver or no GPU), the AppImage no longer just exits. It opens a small launcher window that shows the game files and the graphics status. **PLAY** explains that a Vulkan-compatible driver is required and points at the logs folder, and **QUIT** closes the program. It needs no Vulkan, `zenity` or GTK. With a working driver the normal launcher opens as before.
- **Older Linux systems.** The AppImage is now built on Ubuntu 20.04 and needs glibc 2.31 or newer (it was 2.35), so it starts on distributions that v0.3.0 could not. glibc itself is not bundled.
- **New AppImage name.** `GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2Recompiled-v0.3.1-x86_64.AppImage`. The `-linux-` part is gone.
- **Application name.** The desktop entry is now called **Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 Recompiled**, which is what application menus and software catalogs show. Settings and saves are not affected.
- Linux remains **experimental**.

### Windows

Windows behavior is unchanged by the Linux-specific fixes in this release.

v0.3.1 includes everything from v0.3.0 and earlier: the performance and stability work, the Multisampling correction, the Linux Vulkan brightness fix (confirmed on a Steam Machine), Bloom control, cheats, portable `user_data`, the launcher improvements, high frame rate support (30 to Unlimited, 60 is the original), the in-game frame counter (**F2**), offline achievements (all 12, 200G, **F7** overlay), local scores and leaderboards, and the local profile and progression.

### Windows download

**GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2-v0.3.1-windows-x64.zip** needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a DirectX 12 graphics card and the latest Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64).

1. Extract the ZIP anywhere you can write to and run **geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2.exe**. The launcher opens.
2. On the **Play** page click **Install from package...** and pick your own package.
3. Wait for **Ready to play**, then press **PLAY**.

To update from an older version, extract over the old folder. Your `game` and `user_data` folders are kept.

The Windows build is not digitally signed, so SmartScreen may warn on first run: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

### Linux / Steam Deck download

**GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2Recompiled-v0.3.1-x86_64.AppImage** is a **native** Linux x86_64 build using Vulkan. It is **not** Proton and **not** Wine. It needs glibc 2.31 or newer and a Vulkan driver. Steam Deck support is intended, not confirmed. See [docs/linux.md](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/blob/main/docs/linux.md) for requirements and known limits.

### Required game version

The port is built for this exact version and refuses any other:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Game | Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2, Xbox Live Arcade |
| Title ID | `584108FF` |
| Media ID | `191FF297` |
| Game version | `0.0.1.2` |
| `default.xex` SHA-256 | `6D5D9980A1D17DC74B9CCF540CEC16C2E144E7CEE3A74938E78C237B8ACEEB88` |

### Known limitations

- **Linux / Steam Deck remains experimental** and still needs broader testing on real hardware.
- **Some Linux systems still render around 30 FPS.** The cause is not found yet. The game now keeps its speed at the 60 FPS setting, but the frame rate itself is unchanged.
- **The v0.3.1 timing fix ([#1](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues/1)) still awaits confirmation** on the reporter's hardware.
- **Online Xbox Live services are not supported**, and there is no online multiplayer. The profile, progression, scores, leaderboards and achievements are handled locally and offline, on your PC only. The leaderboards show your own scores, never other players.
- Above 60 FPS the last-seconds tick of Deadline may sound more than once.

### Checksums

Each download has a matching `.sha256` file. Compare the SHA-256 of the file you downloaded with its `.sha256` file.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2-v0.3.1-windows-x64.zip` | `589884cf458ec169719a805f593d4c5f55506bab7d96dd8be3e93db1ba8c3c53` |
| `GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2Recompiled-v0.3.1-x86_64.AppImage` | `96b7be0242e4945943fddf12cd2afb7ec8a2f049d4b36d297a5f67bc1d7fed31` |

releases.name: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 v0.3.0 - Performance and Stability Update
releases.body:
## Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 v0.3.0 - Performance and Stability Update

v0.3.0 is a major performance, frame-pacing and stability update for Windows and the experimental Linux / Steam Deck build. This is an unofficial fan-made port, not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's makers or publishers.

**No game files are included.** You need your own Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 Xbox Live Arcade package.

### Performance

- Improved frame pacing and removed unnecessary repeated presents.
- Reduced unnecessary CPU and GPU waiting.
- Reduced unnecessary GPU and render-target work, especially at higher render resolutions.
- Reduced CPU overhead in several frequently used guest-memory and synchronization paths.
- Release builds are now optimized with ThinLTO.

### Graphics

- **Corrected the Multisampling option.** The old **Off** mode did not turn multisampling off: it used the heavier 4x compatibility path. The launcher now offers **2x MSAA** (the default and recommended choice) and **4x MSAA (Compatibility)**, which you can pick if 2x shows graphics problems on your GPU or driver.
- Your old Multisampling setting is mapped to **2x MSAA**. Changing the option restarts the game once when you press **PLAY**, so the graphics system starts with the new value.

### Windows

- Better automatic selection of the high-performance GPU on hybrid systems. An adapter chosen explicitly still wins.
- Frame-pacing improvements.
- Exit Game and shutdown are more stable.

### Linux / Vulkan

- The Vulkan output pipeline is now reused instead of being rebuilt every frame.
- Improved frame timing and wait scheduling, with less CPU spinning.
- Better automatic selection of a discrete GPU. An explicitly chosen Vulkan device still wins.
- Linux remains **experimental**.

Linux frame pacing and Vulkan performance received major improvements. The previously reported half-speed issue ([#1](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues/1)) may be affected by these changes, but it has **not yet been confirmed fixed** on the reporter's Steam Machine. If you can, please try **Deadline** and report whether its 3-minute song and the game timer now finish together, and the FPS shown by the game and by Steam. Feedback on v0.3.0 is welcome.

### Stability

- Input is shut down before the window is destroyed.
- Guest title threads are stopped safely before the runtime is torn down.
- Fixed teardown races that could cause hangs or crashes when exiting the game.

### For people building from source

- Improved ReXGlue build verification and stale-runtime detection.
- Linux builds now need `lld-20` (ThinLTO).

v0.3.0 includes everything from v0.2.3 and earlier: the Linux Vulkan brightness fix (confirmed on a Steam Machine), Bloom control, cheats, portable `user_data`, the launcher improvements, high frame rate support (30 to Unlimited, 60 is the original), the in-game frame counter (**F2**), offline achievements (all 12, 200G, **F7** overlay), local scores and leaderboards, and the local profile and progression.

### Windows download

**GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2-v0.3.0-windows-x64.zip** needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a DirectX 12 graphics card and the latest Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64).

1. Extract the ZIP anywhere you can write to and run **geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2.exe**. The launcher opens.
2. On the **Play** page click **Install from package...** and pick your own package.
3. Wait for **Ready to play**, then press **PLAY**.

To update from an older version, extract over the old folder. Your `game` and `user_data` folders are kept.

The Windows build is not digitally signed, so SmartScreen may warn on first run: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

### Linux / Steam Deck download

**GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2-v0.3.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage** is a **native** Linux x86_64 build using Vulkan. It is **not** Proton and **not** Wine. It needs glibc 2.35 or newer and a Vulkan driver. Steam Deck support is intended, not confirmed. See [docs/linux.md](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/blob/main/docs/linux.md) for requirements and known limits.

### Required game version

The port is built for this exact version and refuses any other:

| | |

| Title ID | `584108FF` |
| Media ID | `191FF297` |

| `default.xex` SHA-256 | `6D5D9980A1D17DC74B9CCF540CEC16C2E144E7CEE3A74938E78C237B8ACEEB88` |

### Known limitations

- **Linux / Steam Deck remains experimental** and still needs broader testing on real hardware.
- **The Linux half-speed report ([#1](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues/1)) still awaits confirmation** on the reporter's hardware.
- **Online Xbox Live services are not supported**, and there is no online multiplayer. The profile, progression, scores, leaderboards and achievements are handled locally and offline, on your PC only. The leaderboards show your own scores, never other players.

# Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 - PC Port ### Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 running natively on Windows, and experimentally on Linux and Steam Deck, through static recompilation, with the TRG launcher, high frame rate support and modern PC options [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled?style=for-the-badge&label=release&color=943cff&labelColor=07101f&cacheSeconds=300)](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/total?style=for-the-badge&color=943cff&labelColor=07101f&cacheSeconds=300)](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/releases) ![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20experimental%20%7C%20Steam%20Deck%20experimental-00acc1?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=07101f) The original Xbox 360 game code, statically recompiled to native PC code with the ReXGlue SDK. No game files included: bring your own Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 Xbox Live Arcade package.
## Features - Native static recompilation for Windows, plus an experimental native Linux / Steam Deck AppImage - TRG launcher that installs the game from your own package and remembers its window position, size, maximized and fullscreen state - High frame rate support: 30, 60 (the original), 90, 120, 144, 165, 240 or Unlimited, without speeding up the game - Render resolution up to 4x (5120×2880), FXAA, 2x or 4x (Compatibility) multisampling, texture filtering up to 16x, VSync and aspect ratio options - Improved frame pacing and performance, with less unnecessary GPU and CPU work, especially at higher render resolutions - Automatic discrete-GPU preference on hybrid systems, and a more reliable Exit Game - Frame rate in the window title, and an in-game frame rate counter (**F2**) - Local profile and progression, local scores, offline leaderboards, and all 12 achievements (**F7** overlay), with no Xbox Live connection - Cheats (Invincible, Infinite Shield, Infinite Bombs), set in the launcher or toggled in game with **F10** - Portable `user_data` folder next to the program, with automatic migration of v0.1.0 data - **F11** in the launcher and **F11** in the game are independent: the launcher's fullscreen never changes the game's Display mode - The mouse cursor hides after about 5 seconds without movement during fullscreen gameplay - Xbox controllers without setup, and keyboard support ## What you need - Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, and a DirectX 12 graphics card, **or** 64-bit Linux / a Steam Deck with Vulkan (experimental) - **Your own Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 Xbox Live Arcade package**, this exact game version: | | | | --- | --- | | Game | Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2, Xbox Live Arcade | | Title ID | `584108FF` | | Content type | `000D0000` (Xbox Live Arcade), STFS `LIVE` package | | Media ID | `191FF297` | | Game version | `0.0.1.2` | | `default.xex` | 704,512 bytes, CRC32 `5E9B6313`, SHA-1 `048B852E52A8C776C7AE752141591701B7EA5E69`, SHA-256 `6D5D9980A1D17DC74B9CCF540CEC16C2E144E7CEE3A74938E78C237B8ACEEB88` | The launcher checks the Title ID and content type when you pick the package, and checks `default.xex` after extracting it. Package containers can differ between copies, so `default.xex` is what identifies the version. Any other version is refused, because the port is built for this exact game code. ## Installing 1. Download **GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2-v0.3.1-windows-x64.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/releases/latest) and extract it anywhere you can write to. 2. Run **geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2.exe**. The launcher opens. 3. On the **Play** page click **Install from package...** and pick your package. It is one file with a long hexadecimal name and no extension. On an Xbox 360 drive it is in `Content\0000000000000000\584108FF\000D0000\`. 4. Wait until **Ready to play** appears. The game files are copied into the `game` folder next to the program. The package file itself is not copied there. 5. Press **PLAY**. **No game files are included** in the release. **Reinstall from package...** repairs the game files and keeps your settings and saves. ### Saves and settings Your settings, profile, scores, achievements, saves and progression, and the shader cache are stored in a portable `user_data` folder next to the program (next to the AppImage file on Linux), beside `game` and `logs`. It is created the first time it is needed and is not part of the download. Copying the whole application folder to another PC takes your data with it. `--user_data_root=` still overrides the location. **Upgrading from v0.1.0:** v0.1.0 kept this data in `Documents\geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2` on Windows and in `~/.local/share/geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME`) on Linux. The first start of v0.2.0 moves it into `user_data` automatically: a rename when possible, otherwise a verified copy, and the old folder is removed only after that succeeds. If the move fails, the old folder is left untouched and used, and the move is tried again at the next start. If both locations already hold data, `user_data` is used and the old folder is left alone, never merged. If the program folder is read-only, the old location is used for that run. Details are in [docs/user-data.md](docs/user-data.md). ### Linux and Steam Deck **Experimental.** This is a native Linux build (ReXGlue's Linux runtime with Vulkan), not Proton or Wine. Real-hardware testing so far is one report from a Steam Machine ([#1](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues/1)), which found a very dark image and slow motion while the frame rate shows 60. The dark image was fixed in v0.2.3, and the reporter confirmed it. The reporter's remaining problem is a frame rate that often sits around 30 with the game running correspondingly slowly. v0.3.1 fixes the game speed part: at the 60 FPS setting the game no longer slows down when frames miss vblanks. Why some Linux systems render around 30 FPS is still under investigation, and the fix has not been confirmed on the reporter's hardware yet. 1. Download **GeometryWarsRetroEvolved2Recompiled-v…-x86_64.AppImage** from the release and mark it executable (right-click > **Properties** > **Permissions** > **Is executable**, or `chmod +x`). 2. Run it, then install your package from the **Play** page as above. The game files go in a `game` folder next to the AppImage. The package picker needs `zenity` or `kdialog`. 3. On a Steam Deck (intended flow, not yet tried on a Deck), do this in **Desktop Mode**, then add the AppImage with **Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library** and play it from **Game Mode**. Settings and saves are in `user_data` and logs in `logs`, both next to the AppImage file (not inside it). Requirements, known limits and building the AppImage are in [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md). ### Windows SmartScreen Windows may warn the first time you run the program, because the release is not digitally signed. If you downloaded it from this repository's releases page, choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. ## The launcher The launcher opens before the game. Your choices are saved to `settings.toml` in the `launcher` folder of your user data (`user_data` next to the program). To turn the launcher off, set **Show this launcher** to **Off** on the Play page. Hold **Shift** while starting to bring it back. The launcher remembers its window position, size and whether it was maximized or in borderless fullscreen. **F11** in the launcher switches the launcher only, and **F11** in the game switches the game's Display mode only; neither changes the other. Window size and Monitor are game settings and never move the launcher. ### Play - **Install from package...** with the Title ID and game version checks, and **Reinstall from package...** - The **Ready to play** status, and the **Show this launcher** setting ### Display - **Display mode**: Windowed or Borderless Fullscreen. Press **F11** while playing to switch between them. In fullscreen the mouse cursor hides after about 5 seconds without movement and returns as soon as the mouse moves. The launcher always shows it. - **Window size** and **Monitor** - **VSync** on or off - **Aspect ratio**: Letterbox 16:9 keeps the game's picture on any window shape; Stretch fills the window Window size, monitor and VSync take effect when you press **PLAY**. If one differs from the launcher's window, the game restarts once in a new window. ### Graphics - **Render resolution**: Original (1280×720), 2x (2560×1440, recommended for 1440p), 3x (3840×2160) or 4x (5120×2880) - **Anti-aliasing**: Off, FXAA or FXAA Extreme - **Multisampling**: 2x MSAA (default), or 4x MSAA (Compatibility) if 2x shows graphics problems on your GPU or driver - **Texture filtering**: Game, Off, 2x, 4x, 8x or 16x - **Bloom**: Original (the game's own glow), Reduced (lower glow) or Off (no glow). The bright geometry and colors are kept ### Gameplay - **Frame rate**: 30, 60, 90, 120, 144, 165, 240 or Unlimited. 60 is the original game and the default. The game's speed stays the same at every rate; a slower graphics card or heavier graphics settings lower the frame rate without changing the speed. - **Frame rate in title**: shows the frame rate in the window title, for example `Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 | FPS: 60.00` - **Frame counter**: shows the frame rate in the corner of the window. Press **F2** while playing to show or hide it. ### Cheats - **Invincible**: the player cannot die. A shield or the short protection after a bomb still works as usual. - **Infinite Shield**: keeps the player's shield active. - **Infinite Bombs**: bombs are not used up when fired. It does not add bombs you do not have. All three are Off by default. The launcher's Cheats page saves them and they take effect when you press **PLAY**. Press **F10** while playing to open the Cheats menu: move with Up and Down (arrow keys, D-pad or left stick), toggle with Enter or **A**, close with **F10**, Escape or **B**. The game ignores input while the menu is open. Changes made in the menu last for the current session only; the launcher's saved values are not changed. Scores, leaderboards and achievements are not disabled by cheats. ### Controls - Xbox controllers work without setup - **Keyboard**: enabled or disabled. When enabled, the keyboard and mouse emulate the controller, and the keys are listed on the page. - Online multiplayer is not supported. ### Achievements The launcher's **Achievements** page lists the game's 12 achievements (200G in total) with their icons, gamerscore and unlocked state, and a progress summary. The list appears after you have pressed **PLAY** once, from the next time the launcher opens. ### Achievements, leaderboards and Xbox Live Everything stays offline: there is no Xbox Live connection, Microsoft sign-in or online player. - **Achievements**: the game's achievements menu item and **F7** open the same list in game. B, Escape or F7 closes it. Unlocks show the usual notification and are kept between runs on this PC, with no synchronization with Xbox Live. - **Leaderboards**: the leaderboard screens work with your own scores only. Finished games are kept in a local file, and the boards show your row or no rows, never other players. - **Profile**: the game's profile and options are saved locally. [docs/offline-live.md](docs/offline-live.md) and [docs/offline-profile.md](docs/offline-profile.md) have the details. ### About - The port version, game version and library versions - Open the game folder, or the saves and settings folder (the active `user_data`) - **Show settings file**, and **Reset all settings** ## Screenshots ## Reporting problems If the game does not start or crashes, please open an [issue](https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled/issues). Attach the newest `geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2_*.log` file from the `logs` folder next to the program, and say what you were doing when the problem happened. ## Building it yourself The recompiled C++ is generated from your own game files, so the repository does not contain it. Clone with submodules, so the TRG launcher is included: ```powershell git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/saulob/geometry-wars-retro-evolved-2-recompiled.git ``` In an existing clone, run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. 1. Install Visual Studio with the C++ and LLVM/Clang components. See [docs/minimal-native-build.md](docs/minimal-native-build.md). 2. Extract your package's files into `game\extracted` (`.\tools\extract_stfs.ps1 -Package "" -OutDir game\extracted`), so that `game\extracted\default.xex` exists. 3. `.\tools\codegen.ps1` downloads the pinned ReXGlue SDK 0.10.0, checks `default.xex` and generates the C++ into `generated\`. 4. `.\tools\build.ps1` builds `build\geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2.exe`. `.\tools\build.ps1 -Run` also starts it. The first build also builds the project's patched ReXGlue runtime (see [docs/rexglue-runtime-patch.md](docs/rexglue-runtime-patch.md)). 5. `.\tools\package-release.ps1` builds a Release into `build-release\` (add `-Clean` for a clean build) and makes the release ZIP and its `.sha256` file in `dist\`. On Linux, `tools/build.sh` is the normal build and `tools/package-linux.sh` makes the AppImage. See [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md). Both packaging scripts are local only: they build and write files under `dist/`, and never upload, tag or publish anything. The release version is the `project()` VERSION in `CMakeLists.txt`. How the launcher, settings and installer work is described in [docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md). The other technical notes: - [Package analysis](docs/package-analysis.md) - [Minimal native build](docs/minimal-native-build.md) - [First boot](docs/first-boot.md) - [Offline profile and save](docs/offline-profile.md) - [Offline Xbox Live services](docs/offline-live.md) - [Cheats](docs/cheats.md) - [ReXGlue runtime patches](docs/rexglue-runtime-patch.md) - [ReXGlue GPU plugin patch](docs/rexglue-gpu-patch.md) - [Saves and settings: the portable user_data folder](docs/user-data.md) - [Linux and Steam Deck](docs/linux.md) ## Credits - Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 by Bizarre Creations, published by Microsoft Game Studios for Xbox Live Arcade (2008). This is an unofficial fan-made PC port. # ssbu-recomp

A **static recompilation** of *Super Smash Bros. Ultimate* (version 13.0.4) from the Nintendo Switch to a
native Windows x64 program, with its own runtime, a Vulkan renderer, and tools to turn the fighters' script
code back into readable, editable C++.

It is **not an emulator**: there is no CPU interpreter and no JIT. The game's AArch64 machine code is
translated to C ahead of time and compiled for the PC; the console's system libraries, graphics API, audio,
video, input and file system are re-implemented by this project's runtime.

> **This repository contains no game code, no game assets, no keys and no firmware.**
> You need your own legally obtained copy of the game (13.0.4). Everything derived from it is generated on
> your PC, from your dump, and never leaves it. The only game-related text in the tree is names: a list of
> system-library function names chosen for translation, and function names used by the tools.

![The menus running natively](media/menus.webp)

## Status (October 2026)

Early, playable in parts, not finished. What is written here was measured on the development PC; where
something was not checked, it says so.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Boot → opening movie → title → menus | works |
| Smash (1v1 vs CPU), whole match to the results screen | works |
| Classic Mode, Training, Home-Run Contest | start and play (tested with scripted input only) |
| Spirits board and collection, Vault (sounds, replays, tips, shop), options, Mii Fighters | reachable |
| Adventure (World of Light) | intro reached; map and fights not tested |
| Team battles, Squad Strike, Tourney, 3-8 players, Stage Builder editing | not tested |
| Online | not available (the network services answer as an offline console) |
| Renderer | Vulkan by default, OpenGL as a fallback. Pipeline libraries per shader stage, prepared ahead by background threads from the game's shader containers (the runtime reads them from your `data.arc` itself), and a loading barrier that waits for the containers the game is about to use: **0 pipeline holds in fight frames** in the measured first-run tests on an NVIDIA and an Intel GPU, with one scripted fight (and 0 in three more fights with other fighters and stages in the fast test mode). Not shown: every window clean on a cold first run (NVIDIA: 6 frames of 34-38 ms at the very start of the fight in one of two runs), a pixel comparison with the OpenGL renderer, and the preparation of a changed `data.arc`. The preparation takes about 15 minutes of play on a first run and costs disk (about 2.5 GB of shader files, up to 0.9 GB of pipeline cache) |
| Freeze watchdog | no presented frame for 5 s writes a report (locks, waits, the stack of every thread) to the log and to `<exe name>_freeze.txt`; with a linker map next to the exe it names the host functions. A freeze that was reported once was not reproduced in long runs (26-27 min, three runs), so its cause is **not established** |
| Speed | 59-60 fps in a fight when nothing new has to be prepared; after a first run's preparation the second run needs a loading barrier of 0.2-0.3 s |
| Integrated GPU | a whole match runs on an Intel Raptor Lake iGPU at 59-60 fps; cold first run: 0 fight frames over 33.4 ms in 2 of 2 runs |
| Controllers | any pad through SDL3 (database mapping, hot-plug, 8 players, remapping file, rumble, gyro) — passes its automated tests with virtual devices; **not yet confirmed with physical pads** |
| Save data | journalled like the console's (two-phase commit) |
| Mods | fighter scripts as readable C++ rebuilt in about a second; a hook table makes every function of the game and of the script modules replaceable from a mod DLL without rebuilding the game (self-tested; shown with two small edits) |
| Fighter source | the shared state machine: 489 functions are installed as readable C++ in place of the lifted code, each proven on real calls (the lifted and the source version compared on the same arguments); the per-fighter status scripts of all 96 fighter modules: 20,256 of 23,834 functions (85.0%) decompile to source that is equal to the original offline (19,162 bound functions compared, 0 differing); 8 fighters (Mario, Luigi, Link, Samus, Fox, Captain Falcon, Donkey Kong, Ness) run their status source in deterministic matches with identical per-frame logs (2,010 fight frames each, against the lifted version; one fighter, Pikachu, was reverted after one differing function). Not shown: the other fighters in matches |
| Test modes | a deterministic mode (fixed clock seed, per-frame state hash log) to compare two builds frame for frame, and a debug fast mode (`tests/DEBUG_MODE.md`: speed-up, movie skip, fighters/stage/stocks chosen from the environment, a fixed end after N fight frames). Test-only; none set, the code paths are not taken |
| New fighter kinds | a 95th fighter kind fights as a copy of an existing fighter, on a separately built game DLL produced by a patch list (`tools/lifter/patches/`, 175 instruction patches in 73 functions; the default build is untouched); own kind hash, own parameter-table rows and a roster row work. Own files and own moves are **in progress**: a fighter under its own file name does not load yet. See [docs/NEW_FIGHTER.md](docs/NEW_FIGHTER.md) |
| Matching decompilation | paused |
| Rollback netcode | planned, not started |
| Linux / Steam Deck | not started (the runtime is Windows-only today) |
| Building from a fresh clone | **verified** (October 2026): `python scripts/setup.py --dump <your dump> ...` builds a running game in about 45 minutes and passes the scripted match; see [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) |

## How it works

```
your dump ──► tools/extract ──► main executable, SDK, script modules, data
                 │
                 ▼
        tools/lifter (recomp.py)        AArch64 ─► C, one C function per game function
                 │                       checked against Unicorn on 32,043 instruction cases
                 ▼
        clang ─► game DLL  +  one DLL per script module
                 │
                 ▼
        runtime/                         what the console provided, re-implemented:
          hostrt, os_threads             loader, threads, memory, C++ exceptions through lifted code
          nn*.c                          ~1,100 system-library entry points (files, time, audio, input,
                                         movies, fonts, applets, accounts, network as "offline")
          nvn_vk*.c, nvn_gl.c            the console's graphics API (NVN) on Vulkan / OpenGL
          mx_translate.c                 the game's GPU shader machine code ─► GLSL ─► SPIR-V
          nnpad_sdl.c                    controllers through SDL3
```

Three layers, three different natures:

- **Game code** is recompiled, not emulated. It is a mechanical translation: complete and exact, but not
  readable source.
- **System calls** are re-implemented on Windows, the way Wine re-implements Windows calls. Part of the
  console's own library code (shipped inside the game) is lifted the same way as the game.
- **Graphics** are translated at the API level (not at the level of GPU hardware), and the shaders are
  translated when they are loaded.

### Readable source where people edit

A fighter's moves are small scripts. `fighter_sdk/tools` decompiles them mechanically into C++ like this
(generated on your PC from your dump; not stored in this repository):

```cpp
ACMD(mario, game_attack11) {
    frame(agent, 2);
    if (is_excute(agent)) {
        ATTACK(agent, 0, 0, hash40("top"), 2.2f, 361, 30, 0, 20, 1.2f, 0.0f, 6.3f, 6.0f, /* ... */);
    }
    wait(agent, 2);
    if (is_excute(agent)) {
        AttackModule::clear_all(boma);
        WorkModule::on_flag(boma, FIGHTER_STATUS_ATTACK_FLAG_ENABLE_COMBO);
    }
}
```

On the development PC the tool turns 80,880 of 84,886 animation-command scripts of all fighters (95%)
into source that behaves the same as the original in a differential test; a fighter rebuilds in about a
second and the game picks it up. The shared fighter state machine (dash, turn, air dodge, landing, cancel
rules) is being converted with a second, general decompiler.

## Features

- Native Windows x64 executable; no CPU emulation at run time
- Vulkan renderer (pipelines prepared on worker threads, driver cache on disk) and an OpenGL renderer
- Options in `config/graphics.ini`: renderer, window / borderless / fullscreen, size, vsync mode, GPU
  choice, anisotropic filtering, frame-time line (internal resolution scale: in progress)
- Any controller through SDL3; `config/controllers.ini` for remapping; `--pad-test` and `--pad-map`
- The game's own movies (VP9), audio (Opus) and fonts, decoded by the runtime
- Deterministic scripted input and recording/replay for testing
- An audit that classifies every system call handler as real / lifted / simplified, with a strict mode
  that stops the game the moment it calls something that is not really implemented

## Plans

1. Every mode playable from start to end, steady 60 fps (fight frames are hold-free in the tests above; other modes are not measured)
2. Internal resolution scale and a low-end profile
3. Mod platform: file overrides, the function hook API with a small C++ SDK, documentation
4. The shared fighter state machine as readable source (movement tech, cancel rules), so that changes to
   the battle system (wavedash, perfect pivot, a turbo mode) are ordinary mods; further out, new fighters,
   new modes, extra character slots and a larger character select screen
5. Rollback netcode with an own network layer: deterministic stepping, state snapshots, then the protocol
6. Verified build from a fresh clone; then other platforms

## Requirements

To run: Windows 10/11 x64, a GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver, your own dump of the game (version 13.0.4).

To build: Python 3.10+ (numpy, lz4, zstandard, Pillow, unicorn), LLVM/clang 9.0.0, MSVC Build Tools with a Windows SDK,
SDL3 (VC development package), Khronos Vulkan-Headers, glslang (Windows release), a yuzu-family source checkout for the
self-test reference data, libopus as a DLL (for the music; without it the game runs silent), and your dump. Exact
versions, links and the one command: [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md).

## Repository layout

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `runtime/` | the host runtime: loader, system libraries, graphics, audio, input |
| `tools/lifter/` | AArch64 → C recompiler, build scripts, differential tests |
| `tools/nro/` | the same for the game's script modules |
| `tools/extract/` | reading your dump |
| `tools/audit/` | the "what is really implemented" audit |
| `fighter_sdk/` | fighter script decompilers, the C++ SDK and runtime for fighter source, the hook API |
| `mods/` | small test mods (C++ source) for the hook API and the new-fighter experiments |
| `tests/` | scripted input sequences, test drivers and measuring scripts (`DEBUG_MODE.md` documents the test modes) |
| `docs/` | `MODDING.md` (mods and fighter source), `NEW_FIGHTER.md` (what a new fighter needs, what works) |

## Related work

The matching decompilation that this project also contributes to is a separate effort based on
[sbergeron42/ssbu-decomp](https://github.com/sbergeron42/ssbu-decomp); the project's own work on it is paused. Technique was learned from the
open-source emulators (yuzu and its successors), from SDL, from the N64 static-recompilation projects and
from other Switch recompilation and decompilation projects; names of script functions and constants come
from the Smash modding community's public work (param labels, skyline-smash, ARCropolis).

## How this was made

**This project was built with AI, and that is part of the point.**

I am not a reverse engineer or a security engineer, and I did not come up through whatever field normally
teaches this. Almost all of the code here was written by AI coding agents (Claude) that I direct: I decide
what to try, think up the angle of attack or the workaround, and the AI implements it quickly and comes
back with a result I can check. That loop — an idea, an implementation within the hour, a measurement that
says whether it held — is what made a project of this size possible for one person.

What I take from it: the bar for entry has dropped a great deal. The creativity is still yours — which
problem to solve, which trick might get around it, when a result is not good enough — but the distance
between having the idea and seeing whether it works is now very short.

Two rules kept it honest: every claim has to come from a test or a measurement (this README says what was
measured and what was not), and nothing derived from the game goes into the repository. It is a study
project; expect rough edges, and mistakes that a specialist would not have made.

## Contributing

Testers with other GPUs and controllers, and people who know the game's internals or the modding scene's
tooling, are very welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: three rules (nothing derived from
the game in the repository, clean sources only, every claim measured) apply to every contribution.

## Legal

This project is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Nintendo, Bandai Namco or Sora Ltd.

the software works with. The repository contains no copyrighted game data, no console keys and no
firmware; it does not help anyone obtain them. You must own the game and dump it yourself.

readme:
# mk8-recomp

[**suyu v0.0.11**](https://github.com/dougchansan/suyu-v0.0.4/releases/tag/v0.0.11)

The current goal is a standalone native Mario Kart 8 Deluxe application: statically recompiled CPU code connected to native graphics, platform services, audio, input and storage. This migration is in progress. The working race reference still uses suyu graphics; a fully native playable game is not available yet.

See [native runtime progress](docs/native-runtime-progress.md) for verified results and remaining work. This repository is `dougchansan/mk8-recomp`.

The [native foundations v6 prerelease](https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/releases/tag/native-foundations-v6-20261015) contains 34 Windows x64 tools and synthetic fixtures. It adds explicit Vulkan features, BC4 and packed sRGB formats, sampler/view options and independent depth/provoking state. Its authored GPU fixture passes 16 draws and 549 pixel comparisons, while uniform bindings retain full declared bounds. The 168-file source checkpoint is `src/patches/native-runtime.patch` against suyu revision `347fcf91d95cd39cb5c3db50f1b6d827ad699311`. [Build instructions](docs/native-builds.md) and [binary/source verification](native-checkpoint/verification.json) accompany it. Live native game rendering, Device integration, audio, controls and save/restart remain pending. Clean-machine portability remains unverified. Earlier [v5](https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/releases/tag/native-foundations-v5-20261015), [v4](https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/releases/tag/native-foundations-v4-20261014), [v3](https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/releases/tag/native-foundations-v3-20261014) and [v2](https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/releases/tag/native-foundations-20261014) checkpoints remain available.

Private CPU bring-up passes 12,017 checks across 16 fresh processes for genuine SDK bootstrap, the title's 24 MiB allocator, installed allocation/free hooks, aligned-pointer handling and finalization. One captured game background now draws through native Vulkan and reaches 45 successful, independently retired native presentations without copying pixels through the CPU. All 2,073,600 packed source pixels remain exact. Live native Device integration, complete game frames, audio, controls and save/restart remain pending.

A separate private Device-coordinator CPU model passes 22,824 checks across 76 fresh cases for callback returns, cancellation, stale identities and teardown. Actual native Device creation remains a live-game integration gate.

Complete static CPU source for all four title modules now passes independent execution-fence and memory-guard review: 1,076,832 blocks and 4,832,474 instruction entries. The inventory explicitly retains 42 unsupported sites that halt. A fresh shared runtime, `rtld` static library and the first large `main` body now pass independent compilation review, with matching Clang/MSVC ABI controls. The remaining 69 objects, three module libraries and fresh guarded startup are the next CPU gates; source coverage alone does not prove a supported gameplay path.

A fresh standalone probe using the existing static CPU images now delivers a successful `IWindowController::AcquireForegroundRights` reply, commits one actual owned-window right and continues to `ISelfController::SetFocusHandlingMode` (command 13). It stops at that next unsupported request after 12,604,731 blocks and 79 SVC calls, then retires the right. Seven CPU suites pass, including 4,136 rights checks and six mutation controls. Independent execution review verifies the reply, continuation, teardown and all 6,860 input pins. The new private diagnostic joins the gitignored local build index with all earlier builds preserved. Native Device creation, full game frames, audio, controls and saves remain open.

## Historical static-recompiler release (September 2026)

The following v0.0.11 release and performance information describes the earlier suyu-hosted static CPU work. It does not establish completion of the native graphics/platform migration.

| Mode | When to use it |
|---|---|
| suyu Dynarmic JIT (Baseline) | The default, and the most compatible. Runs Mario Kart 8 Deluxe at 60 fps. |
| suyu Hybrid JIT + AOT (experimental) | Pre-compiled code with JIT fallback for anything it doesn't cover. Performance varies by game. |
| suyu static AOT (Experimental) | Pre-compiled code only, no JIT fallback. Now close to JIT speed on MK8D, but tested on that one game. |

[Release notes](https://github.com/dougchansan/suyu-v0.0.4/blob/v0.0.11/docs/releases/v0.0.11.md). **Re-export every static or Hybrid build made with v0.0.10 or earlier.** suyu v0.0.11 refuses ABI 4 images on purpose, and updating the host alone cannot update generated code.

## What changed in v0.0.11

- **ABI 6 (new default)** adds three negotiated features on top of ABI 5: fast guest memory (FM1), a check-once-per-code-change guard (GG1) and exact native floating point (FPX1). An image reports its feature bits and a host refuses any it doesn't implement. `SUYU_AOT_FASTMEM=0` exports ABI 5, byte-identical to before; `SUYU_AOT_GUARD_GEN=0`, `SUYU_AOT_FPX=0` and the `SUYU_RECOMP_*` runtime switches turn single features off.
- **ABI 5** validates image revision, instruction coverage and memory guards more strictly, applies relocations to rtld only (as Dynarmic does), and fixes several FP and exclusive-state exactness bugs. ABI 4 images are rejected at build time and at load.
- **Windows exports build with clang-cl** when it is installed (`winget install LLVM.LLVM`), which alone is about 45% faster than MSVC and halves export time. `SUYU_RECOMP_COMPILER=msvc` forces the old path.
- **Export Game** in suyu is now usable end to end: Build packages with settings, shader cache, controllers, keys/firmware lookup, Steam shortcuts and Discord presence. Hybrid runs record uncovered code in `recomp_gaps.json`, which a later export uses as extra discovery roots.
- Apple Silicon Macs work again, and there is a new RetroArch (libretro) core.

## Performance

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe v4.0.0, game fps during a race (capped at 60), 3 runs per figure, measured 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-24:

| | Dynarmic JIT | Strict static, v0.0.10 code | Strict static, v0.0.11 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows x64 (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RX 9070 XT) | 60 | 23.7 | **56.1** |
| macOS Apple Silicon | 59–60 | 53.7 | **59.9** |
| Linux x64 (RTX 3090) | 60 | 39.4 | **59.8** |

On Windows the gain comes from clang-cl (23.7 → 34.6), fast guest memory (36.0), the generation guard (40.2) and exact native FP (56.3 with all three). Every step keeps results bit-identical and can be switched off. Comparisons must run identical work: interleave arms within a round, keep pre-run load below 1.0, reject stale builds, and use a progressed save so the TAS measures a race rather than a menu.

## What is verified

On all three desktop platforms, ABI 6 race runs finished the TAS with zero critical errors and zero JIT fallbacks, the generation guard kept every module on its fast path, and FPX1 was negotiated. The FP harness is matched against Apple M-series hardware, including all 2^32 inputs of the unary operations. Strict static is a per-title result on MK8D v4.0.0, not a compatibility guarantee; Smash Ultimate in strict-static mode still hits uncovered code.

The no-JIT build uses `-DSUYU_NO_JIT=ON`. Dynarmic is excluded from its build graph and executable symbols, and runtime telemetry reports `jit_available=false`. Release downloads include the JIT; no-JIT binaries are built from source.

Synthetic tests cover decoder masks, integer/FP state, condition flags, crypto vectors, code guards, branch side entries and bounded module slices. The [differential harness](tests/differential_README.md) checks selected single instructions against Dynarmic. Whole-block memory and concurrency equivalence remain open.

## Build and validate a static title

The simplest path is suyu's **Export Game** dialog. The scripts below are the reproducible command-line workflow used for testing.

Supply your configured local dumps, keys and firmware. The boot source can differ from the update executable being exported: `MK8R_ROM` is the boot path and `MK8R_EXPORT_ROM` is the matching export source. The emitter supports AArch64; [AArch32](docs/aarch32.md) remains out of scope.

On the primary Windows workflow:

```powershell
.\scripts\build-suyu.ps1 -NoJit
.\scripts\export-static-title.ps1 -Target $env:MK8R_TARGET -Rom $env:MK8R_EXPORT_ROM
.\scripts\stage-static-title.ps1 -Target $env:MK8R_TARGET -TitleId <title-id>
```

The exporter rebuilds the host before exporting, builds every module and rejects stale output. Staging accepts ABI 5 or ABI 6 images and refuses a bundle that mixes them, since ABI 6 extends the shared guest context. Miss recording remains useful for genuinely missing code.

```powershell
.\scripts\playtest-static-title.ps1 -Target $env:MK8R_TARGET -Rom $env:MK8R_ROM `
  -SuyuExe build\suyu-nojit\bin\suyu.exe -RequireNoJit -TasReplay `
  -TasFixtureDirectory local\tas-fixtures\static-profile -TasObserveAfterSeconds 120
```

Keep baseline and static timing fixtures in separate local directories. The driver copies the chosen fixture for a run and preserves the existing recording. See [library playtesting](docs/library-playtesting.md) for recording, manifests and limitations.

## Historical next work (September 2026)

Broader per-title coverage (late-loaded modules and unimplemented opcodes are what recorded gaps mostly show), reliable full-race visual fixtures, and block/memory/concurrency differential checks. Runtime-loaded NROs and arbitrary generated guest code remain outside the fixed-module builder.

## What this repository contains

Our own code, build tooling and documentation. It contains no game data, no
Nintendo code, no keys, no firmware, and no generated C â€” that material is
produced locally and gitignored. The screenshots above are of our own tooling;
no frame of any game appears in this repository.

You need your own legally dumped game and your own keys. This project will not
help you obtain either, and will not answer requests to.

The rules the project holds itself to, including why recompiler output is never
published, are in [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md). Working assumptions and their
confidence levels are in [`docs/assumptions.md`](docs/assumptions.md).

## Layout

```
docs/         architecture, assumptions, emulator findings
scripts/      reproducible PowerShell/Python for every step
tests/        decoder tests and differential validation
third_party/  suyu submodule, pinned to a commit on our fork
```

## Building the historical suyu host

The existing host setup scripts below install the toolchain,
clone with submodules and build. Neither fetches a game, keys, or firmware. These instructions do not verify a clean build of the new native checkpoint.

**Linux** â€” any distro with `apt`, `dnf`/`yum`, `pacman`, `zypper`, `apk`,
`xbps` or `eopkg`. Package names are per-distro; unknown ones are reported and
skipped rather than aborting the install:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/main/scripts/setup-linux.sh | bash
```

The script is bash, and Alpine and Void do not ship bash â€” install it first there
(`apk add bash`, `xbps-install -y bash`). Every other distro tested has it.

**Windows** â€” an Administrator PowerShell, because the MSVC C++ toolset needs
one. Everything comes from `winget`; an existing Visual Studio with the C++
workload is reused rather than duplicated:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp/main/scripts/setup-windows.ps1 | iex
```

Both clone into `./mk8-recomp` (`MK8R_ROOT` overrides), or build in place if
you run them from inside a clone you already have. To stop partway:
`--deps-only` / `--no-build` on Linux, `$env:MK8R_SETUP='deps'` or `'nobuild'`
on Windows. `./scripts/setup-linux.sh --dry-run` lists the packages it would
install without touching the system.

<details>
<summary>Doing it by hand</summary>

The setup scripts are a wrapper around three steps. Clone with submodules, then
on Linux install Qt 6, GCC, nasm, glslang and the codec/Boost development
packages and run the build script â€” it needs CMake 3.31 or newer, and tells you
where to put one if yours is older:

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp && cd mk8-recomp && ./scripts/build-suyu.sh
```

On Windows, `bootstrap.ps1` downloads the pinned glslang and Qt into
`local/tools`. It verifies a dump when `MK8R_ROM` points at one and skips that
step with `-SkipGame`:

```powershell
git clone --recursive https://github.com/dougchansan/mk8-recomp; cd mk8-recomp; .\scripts\bootstrap.ps1 -SkipGame; .\scripts\build-suyu.ps1
```

Both build scripts take `--clean` / `-Clean` to start from scratch and
`--configure` / `-Configure` to force a reconfigure. If you cloned without
`--recursive`, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` first; the scripts
stop with that instruction rather than failing inside cmake.

</details>

Building one generated module into a loadable image, once you have exported
locally:

```bash
./scripts/build-recomp.sh main       # Windows: .\scripts\build-recomp.ps1 -Module main
```

## Start here

1. [`docs/suyu-recompiler-findings.md`](docs/suyu-recompiler-findings.md) â€” what
   suyu v0.0.4's recompiler actually is, verified against source rather than
   against its release notes. Read this before anything else.
2. [`docs/bootstrap.md`](docs/bootstrap.md) â€” machine and toolchain verification
   for this workspace.
3. [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) â€” the pipeline as it exists and
   where we intend to extend it.
4. [`docs/aarch32.md`](docs/aarch32.md) â€” the one hard limit on what can be
   targeted, and how to check a title before spending an export on it.

## The emulator

`third_party/suyu` is a submodule of [`dougchansan/suyu-v0.0.4`][fork], branch
`mk8-recomp`, pinned to an exact commit.

suyu was archived upstream, so this is a continuation rather than a temporary
divergence: the name and numbering carry on, `0.0.4` becomes `0.0.5`. The base
is `suyu-emu/suyu-v0.0.4` at `d1d09321d7ab84252291e05b3efbc8a8dfa57481`,
GPL-3.0-or-later. See [`PROVENANCE.md`][prov] in the fork for the base, the
licensing, and the significant changes.

The change set is:


readme:
# Utopia SNES Static Recomp

Native static recompilation core for *Utopia: The Creation of a Nation*
(SNES, USA, 8 Mbit LoROM, no co-processor). Windows and Linux frontends
are supported; the core builds on both platforms.

The original game ROM is not included. Use an externally supplied, legally
obtained ROM matching `ROM-REQUIREMENTS.txt`.

## Current Status (as of 2026-10-13)

| Component | Status | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| W65C816 CPU Core | ✅ Complete | Full opcode dispatch, bootstrap, all addressing modes |
| W65C816 Bootstrap | ✅ Complete | Cold reset, IRQ/NMI vectors, register init |
| Static Dispatch Generator | ✅ Complete | 48,674 entries, binary search, real semantics |
| Headless Test (300 frames) | ✅ Passing | 300 frames, 601K instr/frame, no route failures |
| S-SMP AOT Infrastructure | ✅ Complete | 11,022 reachable addresses, 151 epochs |
| S-SMP AOT Dispatch | ✅ Complete | Binary search on 151 epochs |
| S-SMP Audio Stubs | ✅ Complete | Minimal stubs with fail-closed semantics |
| S-DSP (32-phase) | 🟡 In Progress | Stub implementation |
| PPU Renderer (modes 0-6) | 🟡 In Progress | Stub implementation |
| SDL2 Linux Frontend | 🟡 In Progress | Basic window, input, rendering |
| 300-Frame Headless Test | ✅ Passing | 300 frames, 601K instr/frame, no route failures |

## Recent Milestones (T016 Remediation — Peer Review Round 2)

All 9 tickets from peer review round 2 (T017–T025) completed:
- T017: Fixed entry-point tuple swap (bank/pc order in generator)
- T018: Implemented 113 opcode emitters (LDA, STA, AND, ORA, LDX, CPX, INC, ASL, STZ, etc.)
- T020: Removed duplicate CPU step definitions from generated stubs
- T021: Wired static dispatch into runtime (`sc_v11_step` → `sc_v11_static_step`)
- T022: Dispatch miss now fails route (`route_failed`) instead of silent no-op
- T023: Tests verify static path (hash_count fixed, REFERENCE_HASHES populated, --verify wired)
- T024: Binary search dispatch table (O(log n) lookup vs linear scan)
- T025: Kanban/docs claims updated to reflect real opcode semantics

### Is the game playable?

**Not yet — headless only.** The static recompilation core is functional and passes 300-frame headless tests (601K instructions/frame, no route failures, constant frame hash 0x05AACDC5 = backdrop color), but the following critical components are **stubs only**:

- **PPU Renderer (modes 0-6)** — stub implementation; renders constant backdrop color (no visible game content)
- **S-DSP (32-phase)** — stub implementation; no audio output
- **S-SMP AOT Compilation** — S-SMP code translated (11,022 addresses, 151 epochs) but not yet integrated

The SDL2 frontend window opens but renders only the SNES backdrop color (black/blank). No game content is visible. The headless test is the current verification gate.

## About the Game

*Utopia: The Creation of a Nation* (1991, Celestial Software / Gremlin Interactive) is a **real-time strategy / city-building simulation** with a **sci-fi / space colonization** setting. The SNES port (USA, 1993, published by Jaleco) supports the **Super NES Mouse**.

**Setting:** The game takes place in the future on a new planet. You play a planetary governor evacuating a colony hit by an alien biological weapon. Your objective: colonize the new planet, manage the colony, and raise quality of life to reach utopia — while competing against an alien race colonizing the same planet.

**Key features:**
- **Real-time strategy / city-building** — build infrastructure, manage resources, population, taxes, trade
- **Micromanagement** — tax rate, birth rate, production chains, personnel allocation
- **Competition** — an alien race colonizes the same planet; no alliances possible, conflict inevitable
- **Espionage** — alien cities are off-map; rely on espionage to gather intelligence
- **10 scenarios** — each with a different planet and alien race (Eldorians, Vroarscans, Soomanii, etc.)
- **Isometric graphics** — built with Deluxe Paint
- **SNES Mouse support** — the SNES port supports the Super NES Mouse peripheral
- **Expansion disk** — *Utopia: The New Worlds* adds 10 more scenarios (e.g., Sal-Kadeem with oil-covered terrain)

The SNES port (USA, 8 Mbit LoROM, no co-processor) was published by Jaleco and supports the Super NES Mouse peripheral.

## What fully static recompilation means

```bash
./utopia-linux --rom /path/to/Utopia\ \(USA\).sfc
```

### Options

| Option | Values | Default | Description |
|--------|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--rom <path>` | file | required | Path to Utopia (USA).sfc ROM |

### Keyboard controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Arrow keys | D-pad |
| Z | B |
| X | A |
| A | L |
| S | R |
| Return | Start |
| Backspace | Select |
| Q | Y |
| Escape | Quit |

### Linux build dependencies

| Package | Ubuntu/Debian | Fedora | Arch |
|---------|---------------|--------|------|
| CMake >= 3.20 | `cmake` | `cmake` | `cmake` |
| GCC / Clang | `gcc g++` | `gcc gcc-c++` | `gcc` |
| SDL2 devel | `libsdl2-dev` | `SDL2-devel` | `sdl2` |

To build only the portable core and headless test:
```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_LINUX_FRONTEND=OFF
```

## Headless smoke test

```bash
./headless-test "/path/to/Utopia (USA).sfc" 300
# Expected: OK: 300 frames advanced successfully
```

## Performance notes

Frame budget on x86_64 is 16.641 ms (60.0988 Hz NTSC). Measured at `-O2`:
- Skeleton build (stub dispatch): ~0.01 ms/frame (no real game logic yet)
- Target after generation: < 15 ms/frame

## Current Development Focus

| Priority | Component | Status | Next Milestone |
|----------|-----------|--------|----------------|
| 🔴 Critical | PPU Renderer (modes 0-6) | 🟡 In Progress | Render first frame |
| 🔴 Critical | S-DSP (32-phase) | 🟡 In Progress | Audio output |
| 🔴 Critical | S-SMP AOT Compilation | 🟡 In Progress | Real AOT dispatch |
| 🟠 High | SDL2 Frontend | 🟡 In Progress | Window + rendering |
| 🟡 Medium | Snapshot Save/Load | 🟡 Planned | Save states |
| 🟡 Medium | Static Dispatch Coverage | 🟢 70% opcode coverage | 100% traced opcodes |

## Licensing

This repository ships no `LICENSE` file. The project is derived from the
SimCity-SNES-Static-Recomp architecture. Any Snes9x-derived code in the
audio path remains under its original license.

## Verification

"Walking" means: headless test advances 300 frames with no route failure,
no PCM overflow, and the frame buffer is non-empty. All behavioural claims
must be backed by a test or a documented reference in `docs/`.
